section_1.title: From ODEs to PDEs: The Concept of Multi-Dimensional Change
section_1.content: Define PDEs by contrasting them with Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs). Use an animation showing a ball rolling down a track (ODE: change in one variable, time) versus a vibrating drumhead (PDE: change in multiple variables, space and time).
section_1.example: A cat pouncing on a moving dot: ODE tracks the dot's path, while PDE describes the ripples in the water bowl if the dot splashes into it.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of Partial Derivatives
section_2.content: Briefly visualize partial derivatives as 'slicing' a 3D surface. Show a mountain terrain map where we analyze the slope in the North-South direction while holding the East-West position constant.
section_2.example: If a heatmap shows room temperature, the partial derivative with respect to 'x' is how fast the air cools as you walk toward the window.

section_3.title: Core Anatomy of a PDE
section_3.content: Introduce the Heat Equation as the quintessential PDE. Explain the components: the rate of change of temperature (temporal) equals the curvature of the temperature distribution (spatial). Use a color-gradient animation to show how a hot rod reaches thermal equilibrium.
section_3.example: A metal spoon handle heating up when left in a pot of soup; the heat 'flows' from hot to cold to smooth out the temperature differences.

section_4.title: Visualizing the Solution Space
section_4.content: Explain that while ODE solutions are curves, PDE solutions are surfaces or volumes that evolve over time. Use an animation of a vibrating guitar string (Wave Equation) to show how spatial constraints (the fixed ends of the string) define the allowable shapes.
section_4.example: A rubber membrane stretched over a circular hoop; when tapped, the complex, shifting geometric shapes represent the solution surface.

section_5.title: Conclusion: The Language of Nature
section_5.content: Summarize that PDEs are the mathematical framework for fields, signals, and waves. Connect these to real-world technology: fluid dynamics in aircraft design and signal processing in smartphones.
section_5.example: An animation of an airplane wing slicing through air, with streamlines modeled by the Navier-Stokes equations, emphasizing that PDEs are the hidden blueprints of our physical world.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text("- " + line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Shift right to give space for lecture
